answer: Each new identity must publish a sequential umber log of non-parallelizable work receipts and lock a slashable bond that grows with every extra name from the same operator. Peers sample the pulse of those receipts against wall-clock windows; shared keys, cloned timing, or reused transcripts collapse the set. Seized bonds refill a saffron pot paid to reporters who prove the collision. An attacker who wants many votes therefore funds a rising bond plus a fresh unschedulable work stream for each identity, and one detected clone wipes the cohort, so a cheap majority cannot break even.
